historical_run.model: Not reported: none of the image-to-3d, rigging or animation task responses includes a model field. ai_model was omitted on the model stage, which followed the API default; the rigging and animation endpoints have no model selection.
historical_run.note: Two live runs, one per language, on October 19, 2026, from a fresh copy of the repository, started at the same time, on Meshy's new rigging engine. Each consumed 30 credits (image-to-3d, a-pose, remeshed to 30,000, textured with PBR) + 5 credits (rigging, height_meters 1.8) + 9 credits (animations, action_ids [0, 466, 4]), read from consumed_credits. Model stage 95.2-108.5 s from start to finish, rigging 14.5 s, animation 11.0-11.7 s, no queue time; 126.9-140.3 s from the first task's creation to the last task's finish and 133-147 s wall from start to files on disk. Neither run needed a resume.

artifact_inspection.method: Local file byte count and SHA-256; GLB JSON accessors and mesh/material/image/skin/animation arrays; joint names from skins[0].joints; clip names and durations from animations[] and their sampler inputs; material texture slots decoded with gltf-transform and sharp; FBX texture references read from the binary.
artifact_inspection.note: Python run artifacts (pictured). The TypeScript run produced a 5,193,200-byte GLB with 30,819 triangles, 37,306 vertices and the same 24-joint skeleton, and a 5,484,236-byte FBX; the Python FBX is 5,550,524 bytes. Both GLBs hold three animation clips named Idle (4.0 s), Regular_Jump (1.83 s) and Attack (2.8 s), in the order of action_ids, plus one embedded 2048 px base color JPEG and no PBR maps, although the rigging stage now keeps them (see cookbook 05). The clip names are the library key values. Model files are not published by this repository.
